intent: The request is not merely read, it is routed: a gold "chamado" stub tears off the ticket and lands in the queue slot, so "encaminha" is a gesture, not a label.
hero: u10-stub — the gold #F4B400 ticket stub carrying the word "chamado", the only saturated object in the frame, travelling the full width and landing in the slot

objects.drift: x -6px, y -5px, scale +0.004 accumulated f0->f34, folded into the SAME curve as the entrance (kit resolve(): tail runs from enter*0.5 to frame 34), so velocity never reaches zero after the settle. 0.24px/frame at the cut.
objects.enter: f0, 9f enter, from {y:+18px, scale:0.972, opacity:0} — a short drop-and-settle, no bounce. Same from-state as u10-stub so the tear-off still reads as one object during f0-f9.
objects.exit: held to cut (cut is dry; the card is the last frame's anchor)
objects.notes: x,y = top-left. Inner padding 36px -> inner box x116..468. NOT the kit Card component (its 58px title and 920 default width do not fit a 424px ticket) — use Plate + custom body. z=0 (behind stub and rail).
objects.what: White ticket plate (r36, hairline border rgba(28,26,24,.14), lift shadow) — the source document. Container for the dot, the 4 skeleton bars and the perforation; it is the biggest mass but has the lowest contrast, so the eye enters here and is handed to the gold stub.

objects.notes: Slightly darker than the body bars: this is the hierarchy cue that reads as 'a document', not a loading spinner.

objects.notes: Stagger continues 1f apart (f3/f4/f5/f6) — inside the kit's 4f stagger unit, group resolves by f14.

objects.notes: The tear line stays behind after the stub leaves — that residue is what makes the stub read as torn, not as a moved chip. It also distinguishes this card from the u09 inbox card and the u11 invoice card.

objects.exit: held to cut inside the slot
objects.notes: Exact knots (local frames, offsets from the seat x116/y394): X = curve([[0,0],[9,-2],[12,-7],[17,300],[23,500],[28,516],[34,520]]); Y = curve([[0,18],[9,1],[12,-1],[17,-15],[22,-4],[26,1],[30,1.5],[34,2]]); SCALE = curve([[0,0.972],[9,1.0],[19,0.985],[27,1.0],[34,1.005]]); ROTATE = curve([[0,0.5],[10,0],[16,-0.9],[22,0.3],[28,-0.2],[34,-0.5]]). internal_beats.event: Ticket plate enters (from y+18, scale 0.972, opacity 0) — the document lands; the stub enters with it as one object
Card internals begin to stagger: dot (f2), title bar (f3), body bars (f4, f5, f6) — one frame apart, top to bottom
Destination slot enters from the right (x+16, scale 0.98) — the queue position now exists before anything travels
Perforation draws left-to-right (scaleX 0.35 -> 1.0); the ticket is now legible as a tear-off
Slot placeholder bar fades in — the destination is 'empty' and waiting
TEAR: the stub reaches its 7px left pull-back and launches — the single gesture of the beat; the rail begins to write on across the gap
Stub at the apex of the 15px arc, 300px travelled (58% of the route) — the throw reads as weight, not as a slide
Shine begins its pass on the stub
Stub crosses the seat line (y offset returns through 0) and the slot's border starts turning gold — landing and receipt are one event
Stub seats inside the slot (98% of x travel, inset in the queue position)
Slot border fully gold (2px) AND the shine pass completes — the last new idea of the beat
Drift only from here: card -6/-5px, stub +520px on its spline, slot -3/-2px, rail -4/-3px, perforation scaleX creeping
CUT — settled frame: every element still moving on its own continuous spline, none frozen, no motion arriving

sfx_cues.why: The stub tears off the perforation: percussive onset on the gesture's first frame, so the tear is heard and not only seen. Under the voice, short, low level.

The stub seats in the slot and the border turns gold — the payoff of the beat, landing under the word 'chamado'. A short UI click, not a whoosh: the travel already reads visually and this format does not mark canvas motion with transition sound.

risks: Busy-ness: 35 frames carry 4 events (ticket in, slot in, tear-off, receipt). If it plays as noise, drop the f12 snap first, then the rail write-on — never the arc, which is what makes the travel read as a throw instead of a slide.
The gold switch completes at f27, i.e. 7 frames before the cut; if that still reads as a late new idea, move the border morph to f21->f25 (before the touchdown) so the frame is fully settled by f27.

The stub's 520px x-drift after landing pushes it 4px off-centre inside the slot. Invisible at 1080 wide, but if the slot is tightened, land the stub at 512 and let the drift carry it to 520 rather than resizing the slot.

The shine and the gold border are two light events in 4 frames. Keep the shine at <=0.38 alpha and 8 frames; if it competes with the border, cut the shine — the border is the one that carries meaning.

The perforation is the only thing that makes the card read as a ticket rather than a skeleton loader. If the dashes render muddy at this scale, widen the dash to 14/10 and raise it to rgba(28,26,24,.26) rather than deleting it.

Palco B compliance is structural (StageB clips at y=960), but verify the still at f6 by sampling alpha: the lowest content is the card at y=510, so the reserved caption band y=700..960 must be 100% alpha 0.
